book.name: Kids on Brooms
book.tagline: Magic school adventures for students and faculty alike.
book.blurb: Kids on Brooms is a collaborative roleplaying game about a magical school, built on the Kids on Bikes engine. Every character is a caster with a wand, a broom and a familiar; there are no spell lists—if it could be done with magic, you can try to do it with magic, and the GM builds each spell's difficulty from its magnitude, area, duration and your experience with it.

ageGroups.name: Underclass
ageGroups.notes: Fast and likeable. Write your favorite class on your sheet and name the teacher who teaches it. Cannot start the game with Master of…; could be Studied in… one type of magic by spending both Strengths.

ageGroups.name: Upperclass
ageGroups.notes: Pugnacious and in their prime. Trained in… one type of magic of your choice. Write your favorite class and name its teacher. Could start as Master of… a type of magic by spending both Strengths.

ageGroups.name: Faculty
ageGroups.notes: Studied in… one type of magic of your choice. Write your favorite class to teach (or your favorite class as a student) and name your best student. Could gain Master of… by spending one Strength at creation.

rules: Begin the game with 3 Adversity Tokens; add 1 each time you fail a roll.
You start with your grade Strength (Innocence / Trained in… / Studied in…) and two more, plus two Flaws.
Grade bonuses: Underclass +1 Flight & Charm; Upperclass +1 Fight & Brawn; Faculty +1 Brains & Grit. Bonuses never cause a Lucky Break.

Every spell is a Spell Check: roll the Stat Die for that type of magic plus a d4 Magic Die, add wand and Strength bonuses, and compare to a difficulty the GM builds from magnitude + area + duration + experience.
The GM must tell you a spell's difficulty before you decide whether to cast it.
Your wand gives +1 to two different types of magic: one from its wood, one from its core.
Your broom's benefit only applies while you are physically riding it.
Familiars allow limited one-way psychic communication and can carry out simple tasks, decided narratively.
Class Schedule: pick 3 classes; take up to 2 marks per session. 2 marks = Trained in… (+1), 6 marks = Studied in… (+3), 10 marks = Master of… (+5).
Casting magic on an unwilling PC or NPC is a contested Spell Check; killing another character other than in self defense turns your character into an NPC.
Species other than human are mechanically identical to humans; they change only how you roleplay.

tropes.name: Aloof Teacher
questions: How much of your aloof persona is sincere and how much of it is affected?
Who do you feel a real connection with, and do they know?

tropes.name: Bullheaded Muscle
questions: What's your go-to way of showing just how strong you are?
Despite your muscle and reputation, you're incredibly gentle in which one part of your life?

tropes.name: Charismatic Slacker
questions: Why don't you want to work as hard as everyone else seems to want to?
What's one part of your life where you do put in much more effort?

tropes.name: Daring Athlete
questions: What's your greatest athletic achievement?
What's the worst injury you've caused someone else to suffer?

tropes.name: Doting Caretaker
questions: What non-teaching role do you play at the school?
What did you do that barred you from teaching magic at the school?

tropes.name: Famous Teacher
questions: What earned you your fame?
What aspects of your fame are unwarranted?

tropes.name: Firstborn Caster
questions: How did you first discover your magical powers?
How did your non-magical family react when you manifested your powers?

tropes.name: Funny Klutz
questions: What's your go-to joke?
Who do you wish would take you more seriously than they do?

tropes.name: Golden Child
questions: Some people think you're the chosen one. Why do you know they're wrong?
Even though almost everyone loves you, who seems to despise you?

tropes.name: Haughty Descendant
questions: What famous or infamous thing is your family known for in the magic world?
Why are you afraid you won't be able to live up to your family's reputation?

tropes.name: Haunted Survivor
questions: What is the tragedy that haunts you?
What strength has that tragedy given you that most others lack?

tropes.name: Offbeat Eccentric
questions: What do you believe in that no one else seems to?
What would it mean to find someone who believes you?

tropes.name: Perfect Prefect
questions: What do you love about getting to guide younger students in your house?
What part of being a prefect do you still struggle with?

tropes.name: Reliable Bestie
questions: Why are you so bonded to your best friend?
When do you wish you were the center of attention rather than the sidekick?

tropes.name: Teacher's Pet
questions: What tricks do you use to get teachers to like you?
Which teacher seems to despise you?

tropes.name: Unlikely Ally
questions: Why is it surprising that you're working with this group?
Why do they think you're working with them? Why are you actually working with them?

tropes.name: Reluctant Oracle
questions: What troubles have your visions prevented?
What confusing vision of the future haunts you?

tropes.name: Wacky Prankster
questions: What's the best prank you've ever pulled?

tropes.name: Withdrawn Bookworm

strengths.name: Cool Under Pressure
strengths.description: You may spend an Adversity Token to take half of your die's value instead of rolling on a Snap Decision.

strengths.name: Easygoing
strengths.description: Gain 2 Adversity Tokens when you fail a check.

strengths.name: Gifted
strengths.description: If you make a check involving the Magic Die that fails, you may spend 1 AT to reroll the Magic Die.

strengths.name: Gross
strengths.description: You have some kind of gross trick or spell (loud, quiet, smelly… up to you) that you can do on command.

strengths.name: Guardian
strengths.description: When defending another player or an NPC, always roll both your stat die and the magic die, then add them together, even if you're not using magic to do it. If your check fails, you may reroll the magic die.

strengths.name: Handy
strengths.description: You gain the benefits of using your wand without having to wield it.

strengths.name: Heroic
strengths.description: You do not need GM's permission to spend Adversity Tokens to ignore Fears.

strengths.name: Innocence
strengths.description: Once per session at the GM's discretion, you may spend 2 AT to convince an adult to not get you in trouble for a minor transgression.

strengths.name: Intuitive
strengths.description: You can spend 1 AT to ask the GM about your surroundings, an NPC, or the like. The GM must answer honestly.

strengths.name: Loyal
strengths.description: Each of the AT you spend to help your friends gives them a +2 instead of a +1.

strengths.name: Lucky
strengths.description: You may spend 2 AT to reroll a stat check. It does not allow you to reroll the Magic Die.

strengths.name: Prepared
strengths.description: Spend 2 AT to just happen to have one commonplace item with you (GM's discretion).

strengths.name: Psychic Link
strengths.description: You have complete two-way psychic communication with your familiar at any distance.

strengths.name: Resilient
strengths.description: When spending AT to boost a check against a spell that targets you, each AT is worth +2 instead of +1.

strengths.name: Skilled at...
strengths.description: Choose a skill (GM's discretion). You are assumed to succeed when making even moderately difficult checks involving this skill. If the GM determines that you do need to roll for a more difficult check, add up to +3 to your roll.

strengths.name: Spell Slinger
strengths.description: If you fail a spell check, add +3 to the negative number. You will still lose the roll no matter what but could reduce your loss to -1.

strengths.name: Trained in...
strengths.description: Choose one type of magic. Gain +1 to all spells of that type.

strengths.name: Studied in...
strengths.description: Choose a type of magic that you are already Trained in. Gain +3 to all spells of that type. This bonus is not cumulative with the bonus for the "Trained in..." Strength.

strengths.name: Master of...
strengths.description: Choose a type of magic that you are already Studied in. Gain +5 to all spells in that type. This bonus is not cumulative with the bonus for the "Trained in..." or "Studied in..." Strengths.

strengths.name: Tough
strengths.description: If you lose a combat roll, add +3 to the negative number. You will still lose the roll, but can reduce your loss up to -1.

strengths.name: Treasure Hunter
strengths.description: Spend 1 AT to find a mundane but useful item in your surroundings.

strengths.name: Unassuming
strengths.description: You can spend 2 AT to not be seen, within reason (GM's discretion).

strengths.name: Wealthy
strengths.description: May spend money as though they were a higher Age Bracket. A wealthy underclass student has the disposable income of a typical upperclass student; a wealthy upperclass student has that of a typical faculty member. Wealthy adults don't have to worry too much about money—they can buy anything they need and can likely spend their way out of a lot of situations.

strengths.name: Wild Speak
strengths.description: You can communicate with any animal whose species you have knowledge of.

items.name: Defense Against Malicious Magic
items.description: This class teaches the basics of defending yourself against hexes, jinxes, and other malicious forms of magic.

items.name: History of Magic
items.tag: Fight, Flight, Brains, Brawn, Charm, Grit
items.description: This class is an overview of the important discoveries and figures of the magical world.

items.name: Potions
items.description: This class covers the ingredients and techniques required to create magical potions and tinctures.

items.name: Divination
items.description: This class provides insight into the many various methods of seeing into the future. Advanced studies can also involve sharing your own visions and memories with them.

items.name: Astronomy
items.description: This class covers the heavenly bodies, their movements, and the impact they have on the magical world.

items.name: Numerology
items.description: This class teaches the magical properties of numbers and their sequences, and how they're used to understand the theoretical building blocks of magic.

items.name: Charms
items.description: This class covers the use of magic on inanimate objects and the use of non-harmful magic on people.

items.name: Brooms
items.description: This class focuses on the use of magical brooms in transportation and sport.

items.name: Summoning
items.description: This class teaches the methods and dangers of using magic to summon objects or creatures from nothing.

items.name: Transfiguration
items.description: This class covers the proper spells used to transform both inanimate objects and living beings into other things.

items.name: Curiosity
items.description: Typically, underclass students will be motivated by their curiosity.

items.name: Fitting in or a romantic relationship
items.description: Upperclass students will often be motivated by social factors like fitting in or finding and maintaining a romantic relationship.

items.name: Protecting what they have
items.description: Faculty will be motivated by holding on to or protecting what they have, whether that's a business or family.

items.name: Something or someone lost
items.description: All grades can be motivated by something or someone that they've lost.

items.name: The unknown and what they can't see
items.description: Underclass students usually fear things that, rationally, they shouldn't and don't fear things that they ought to. Kids are generally not ashamed of their fears.

items.name: Social isolation, losing friends, embarrassment
items.description: Upperclass students are all over the place; some keep childhood fears but are tight-lipped about them. Often they're more scared of social isolation, losing friends, or embarrassing themselves.

items.name: Things being taken from them
items.description: Adults are typically afraid of things being taken from them—their families, their homes, or their livelihoods—and of realistic things going wrong.

magicTypes.text: Attack enemies, break curses, or blast through obstacles. Common spells include disarming an opponent, causing a target harm, or making something explode.
magicTypes.classes: Defense Against Malicious Magic, History of Magic, Potions

magicTypes.text: Hide yourself, avoid being hurt, or use your broom to navigate. Common spells include deflecting dangerous magic, moving in magical ways, or blending into your surroundings.
magicTypes.classes: Defense Against Malicious Magic, Transfiguration, History of Magic, Brooms

magicTypes.text: Reveal something hidden, understand something mysterious, or see into a different place in space or time. Common spells include finding hidden passages, astral projection, or decoding magical messages.
Move an object or keep something protected. Common spells include levitation, magically locking doors, or binding opponents.

Influence someone's thinking, create an illusion, or modify your appearance. Common spells include disguising yourself, being allowed into somewhere you normally aren't, or projecting images from your mind into reality. Magically influencing an unwilling person's emotions is against the rules at most schools.
Keep someone safe either mentally or physically. Common spells include blocking your mind from being peered into, dispelling magic that's already been cast, or healing someone who has been hurt.
magicTypes.classes: History of Magic, Potions, Defense Against Malicious Magic

failure.text: The character seems to cast the spell effortlessly, like this is a spell they could do in their sleep. The spell functions perfectly.
The character casts the spell quite impressively; to anyone watching it seems like a spell they have mastered. The spell functions perfectly.
The character casts the spell but not impressively. It works, but it's clear they put serious effort into making it succeed. The spell functions as expected.
The character casts the spell—but just barely. The strain is clear to everyone watching, and the spell might not function perfectly, but it gets the job done.
The spell simply fails. It may appear about to work but then does not. No impact on the story beyond the caster not achieving their stated goal.
The spell fails in a benign burst of magic. At the GM's discretion there may be minor, incredibly brief unexpected effects—slightly embarrassing if anyone is there to witness them.

The spell fails in a dangerous burst of magic. There will be minor effects as above and, at the GM's discretion, the spell might work but on the wrong target. Some short-term impact on the direction of the game.

The spell fails in an incredibly dangerous way. Bad effects as above and perhaps quite a bit worse; such a failure should alter the course of the game. This only happens when a character is incredibly reckless with magic.

quickRules.title: Grades
quickRules.text: Underclass (14 & younger): +1 Flight & Charm, free Innocence. Upperclass (15–20): +1 Fight & Brawn, free Trained in… one type of magic. Faculty (21+): +1 Brains & Grit, free Studied in… one type of magic. Grade bonuses apply to stat checks and never cause a Lucky Break.

quickRules.title: Starting Character
quickRules.text: Pick a Trope (or build from scratch), choose your grade, your grade Strength plus two more Strengths, two Flaws, a familiar, a wand, a broom, a favorite class, a motivation, a fear and your Schoolbag. Start with 3 Adversity Tokens.

quickRules.title: Types of Magic
quickRules.text: Every spell uses one stat: Fight (attack, break curses), Flight (hide, evade, broom flying), Brains (reveal, understand, scry), Brawn (move or protect objects), Charm (influence, illusion, appearance), Grit (protect minds and bodies, dispel, heal). The GM decides which type a spell is.

quickRules.title: Wands
quickRules.text: Choose a wood and a core. Each gives +1 to magic checks of one type, and the core's type must differ from the wood's. Any two-part focus object can stand in for a wand. Handy lets you use the wand's benefits without wielding it.

quickRules.title: Brooms
quickRules.text: Each brand has a rider adjective and a mechanical benefit (see the broom table, p.25). The benefit only lasts while you are physically on the broom, and a damaged broom won't work as well. Flying where non-casters can see you exposes magic to the outside world.

quickRules.title: Familiars
quickRules.text: Any animal small enough to carry (GM's permission for anything unusual). You have limited one-way psychic communication and it can perform simple tasks, decided narratively rather than by rolls. Psychic Link upgrades this to two-way at any distance.

quickRules.title: Spell Checks
quickRules.text: 1) Describe what the spell does. 2) The GM sets the type of magic and builds the difficulty: magnitude + area + duration + experience (one modifier from each table). 3) Roll the Stat Die for that type plus the d4 Magic Die and add wand, Strength, grade and Adversity Token bonuses. 4) Meet or beat the difficulty and the spell does exactly what you wanted; there is no extra benefit for beating it by a lot.

quickRules.title: Magic Die
quickRules.text: Every Spell Check adds a d4 Magic Die to the stat die. Gifted lets you spend 1 AT to reroll it after a failed magic check; Lucky rerolls the stat check but never the Magic Die. Guardian always adds the Magic Die when defending someone, even without magic.

quickRules.title: Know the Difficulty First
quickRules.text: Because failed spells can go badly wrong, the GM must tell you the spell's difficulty before you decide whether to cast it. Spell Checks are normally rolled, not taken as Planned Actions.

quickRules.title: Spell Failure
quickRules.text: Compare (roll + modifiers) − difficulty on the spell results chart (p.56–57). −1 to −4 simply fails; −5 to −9 a benign burst; −10 to −14 a dangerous burst that may hit the wrong target; −15 or lower an incredibly dangerous failure that alters the game. Spell Slinger adds +3 to the negative number, to a minimum loss of −1.

quickRules.title: Magic Against Living Creatures
quickRules.text: Casting on an unwilling PC or NPC: both caster and target make a Spell Check for the same spell and the difference is read on the Injuries chart. Unprovoked magical attacks are among the gravest crimes; killing another character other than in self defense makes your character an NPC. Supervised duels cap injury at 'attacker greater by 3'.

quickRules.title: Injuries
quickRules.text: Defender's roll ≥ attacker's: uninjured, defender narrates. Attacker +1 to +3: hurt but temporary. +4 to +6: fairly hurt, needs medical attention soon. +7 to +9: badly hurt, straight to the infirmary or permanent damage. +10 or more: dead or nearly dead, attacker controls the narrative. There are no hit points and no pulled punches.

quickRules.title: Potions
quickRules.text: With time and a lab, brew a magical effect for later. The GM sets a difficulty (+5 without components) and may add requirements: a rare ingredient, brewing time, exhaustion, or a specialized lab. Roll as a Snap Decision; the GM may allow a Planned Action for simple potions you've studied or have a recipe for. Using a potion erases it from your Schoolbag.

quickRules.title: Class Schedule
quickRules.text: Choose 3 classes. After each session take up to 2 marks (max 1 per class) in classes you used. 2 marks: Trained in… (+1) a magic type the class teaches. 6 marks: replace with Studied in… (+3). 10 marks: replace with Master of… (+5) and the class is complete. Bonuses don't stack.

quickRules.title: Fears
quickRules.text: When faced with your fear you must make Snap Decisions, cannot spend AT to help friends, and may suffer up to −3 on all checks (−1 persistent but irrelevant, −2 persistent and possibly relevant, −3 persistent and overwhelming). With GM permission (or Heroic) spend 1 AT per −1 penalty to ignore the fear for the scene. Valiance 2400 riders ignore fears.

quickRules.title: Schoolbag
quickRules.text: A lightweight magical pouch that compresses small objects: spell supplies, potions, even a broom—nothing bigger fits. Figuratively, also list the advantages you 'hold' over others (family prestige, resilience) as roleplaying cues without mechanical effect.

quickRules.title: Money
quickRules.text: Underclass students have almost no money beyond what they're given. Upperclass students can cover necessities for a few days and maybe a top-of-the-line broom. Faculty can, within reason, buy what they want. Anyone wealthy—even a well-paid adult—must take the Wealthy Strength.

quickRules.title: Safety
quickRules.text: Set boundaries before play and use a safety tool: the book recommends a modified X-card (knock on the table), Script Change (rewind / pause / fast forward) or Lines & Veils, and checking in with everyone whenever the table seems frustrated.
